display.purpose: Page titles, card/section headers, and the two authentication surfaces (login, session-expired). Never Sheet titles, dropdown content, body, or stat values.

body.purpose: All running content: table cells, form values, descriptions, Sheet titles, dropdown menus.

label.purpose: Field labels' captions, stat-tile labels, record-field labels, pagination text.

data-mono.purpose: Reserved, not yet applied anywhere — intended for AWB/tracking-code style data.

shadows.name: ambient-rest
shadows.purpose: Tailwind default `shadow` — Cards, primary/secondary/destructive buttons at rest.

shadows.name: ambient-subtle
shadows.purpose: Tailwind `shadow-sm` — Inputs, Select triggers, outline Button.

shadows.name: overlay-lifted
shadows.purpose: Tailwind `shadow-lg`/`shadow-md` — the Sheet panel and dropdown/select popovers, reserved for floating overlays.

shadows.name: auth-gate-lift
shadows.purpose: `shadow-xl shadow-primary/5` — the Login card and the session-expired Dialog only. The one ink-tinted, more dramatic shadow in the system; never used on ordinary in-page cards.

motion.name: sheet-close
motion.purpose: Sheet slide-out on close — deliberately faster than open.

motion.name: color-transition
motion.purpose: All hover/active background and text-color shifts (buttons, nav items, badges, dropdown items) — the system's primary motion vocabulary besides the Sheet slide.

motion.name: login-cta-nudge
motion.purpose: The login button's trailing arrow icon nudges right on hover — a confirmed one-off for the single highest-stakes action in the app, not a general button pattern.

components.description: The single highest-priority action on a screen.

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Signature component: a neutral pill with a color-coded dot, never a saturated fill — status is always confirmed by the adjacent text label, not by color alone.
components.css: .ds-status-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 2px 10px; background: #e9e9ed; color: #161821; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; border-radius: 4px; } .ds-status-dot { display: inline-block; width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #0f766e; }

components.name: Icon-Decorated Input
components.description: The auth-surface field style: a leading icon inside the field, hairline border, thin focus ring. Not yet used outside Login/reauth.

narrative.overview:
This is the visual language of a courier branch counter's paper ledger, digitized: a warm, unbleached paper background, deep-indigo ink for text, and a restrained set of status colors that behave like rubber-stamp categories, not marketing accents. It exists to be read quickly and correctly under time pressure by dispatchers, counter staff, and finance clerks — not to persuade or delight. Density and legibility come first; the main "expression" the system allows itself is Space Grotesk's slightly more geometric, confident display face on titles, section headers, and the two authentication surfaces (login, session-expired), which keeps the interface from reading as generic gray SaaS while staying almost entirely out of the way in working content.

The palette is deliberately calmer than a typical categorical status system: every status hue was tuned to clear WCAG AA contrast and CVD-safe adjacent-pair separation first, vivid-and-legible-as-a-swatch second. Status is never carried by color alone — every colored dot or badge ships with its text label next to it, because color is a confirmation signal here, not the message itself.

Two rejections are explicit and confirmed, not just absent: no camera/scanner chrome or courier-brand marketing gloss (this is Operate-mode software, not a storefront for the courier company), and no invented brand identity — the product has no confirmed name or logo yet, so this system stays intentionally generic/white-label rather than pretending to a personality it hasn't earned.

This system is still mid-build, and it shows two small, real seams rather than one seamless language, both called out honestly rather than papered over: dashboards use two different shapes for a tinted-emphasis icon badge, and the global header search bar is a visual placeholder with no function behind it yet.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper background + deep indigo ink, not black-on-white or cool gray-on-white.
A muted, WCAG-AA-first status palette — legible over loud, colorblind-safe over saturated.
Space Grotesk display type for titles, section headers, and the two auth surfaces; IBM Plex Sans everywhere else, including Sheet titles.
Almost flat: one soft default shadow for in-page surfaces, a second tinted lift reserved for the two auth surfaces.
Every detail/create view opens as a right-side Sheet, never a routed page.

rules.name: The Label-Always Rule
rules.body: No status is ever communicated by color alone. StatusBadge always pairs its colored dot with the status's text label.

rules.name: The Tint-From-Token Rule
rules.body: A colored icon-chip or highlight-panel background is always an existing status or accent token at reduced opacity, never a new ad hoc hex value. The chip's shape (circle vs. square) is not yet settled across dashboard components — a known open inconsistency, not a hidden rule.

rules.name: The Sheet-Stays-Plain Rule
rules.body: Sheet titles use the plain body face, not Space Grotesk, with no exceptions in shipped code. The session-expired Dialog is a different surface type and does use the display face — don't generalize its choice back onto Sheets.

rules.name: The Flat-Ledger Rule
rules.body: Depth exists only to separate an overlay (Sheet, dialog, dropdown) from the page beneath it, or to mark the two authentication gate surfaces (login, session-expired) with a tinted shadow. A surface in the normal document flow never gains a shadow it didn't already have at rest.

dos: Do use Space Grotesk for page titles, card/section titles, and the two authentication surfaces; every other piece of text — including Sheet and dropdown content — stays in IBM Plex Sans.
Do pair every status color with its text label — never color as the sole signal.
Do source any tinted icon-chip or highlight-panel background from an existing status or accent token at reduced opacity, never a new hex value.

Do open every detail/create/edit view as a right-side Sheet backed by a Zustand panel store; reserve routed pages for list/index views, and the centered Dialog exclusively for app-level interruptions like session expiry.
Do verify a new status or semantic color against WCAG AA contrast and CVD-safe adjacent-pair separation before adding it — this is a binding standard, not best-effort.
Do hide a nav item or gated action entirely when the user lacks the permission, rather than showing it disabled.
Do wire up real search functionality before extending the header search bar's visual treatment — it renders today but does nothing.
donts: Don't add a shadow to an at-rest surface (card, tile, table row) that doesn't already have one — depth is reserved for overlays and the two auth-gate surfaces only.
Don't introduce a second monospace or display typeface; IBM Plex Mono is already reserved (unused) for AWB/tracking-code data.
Don't give Cards the base 6px --radius scale; their 12px rounded-xl is an intentional, confirmed exception.
Don't invent a brand name, logo, or marketing personality for this product — it is confirmed unnamed/white-label.
Don't build nested/collapsible sidebar nav groups speculatively — the flat list is deliberate until a real feature needs sub-items.

Don't copy the tinted-emphasis icon badge's shape from just one existing dashboard component and assume it's settled — RateTiles (circle) and FinancialSummary (square) disagree; pick one deliberately.
